zeno.name: Zeno
zeno.first_appearance: Hulk vs. Hercules: When Titans Collide Vol 1 1
zeno.origin: Zeno was a giant blinded by a lightning bolt from Zeus during the Gigantomachy and was then spared from an imprisonment in Tartarus. He and fellow giant Callias were feasting on a boar outside the door when the Hulk arrived. Assuming he was a fellow giant they invited him to eat, and the trio feasted for a bit until Ares attacked them for "stealing" his hunt. The Hulk threw Ares into the gate cracking it and the pair of giants encouraged him to attack the Olympians on Mount Olympus in vengeance. Later, when Cronus escaped and the Olympians arrived, Hercules slayed both Zeno and Callias.

zenogg.name: Zenogg
zenogg.origin: Zenogg was the ruler of the planet Planet Zenn, a planet that had not developed the concept of defense and so when their neighboring planet Quo began to develop starflight, they worried about being invaded. To prevent this, Zenogg contacted the Star Raiders, a group of escapees from the prison planet of Torgo who successfully engaged in space piracy. Zenogg asked them to attack and plunder the planet Quo, and the Star Raiders accepted also because it was well known that the inhabitants of Zenn were unable to lie and Zenogg had declared that the inhabitants of Quo were widgets. When they attacked the planet Quo however, the Star Raiders found themselves facing giants who easily captured all of the Star Raiders except their leader Brock. Escaping on the Star Raiders' spaceship, Brock contacted Zenogg asking him how it was possible that an inhabitant of Zenn could have deceived them, but Zenogg replied that he had not deceived them but that he had told the truth because for the inhabitants of Zenn all were gods midges since they were gigantic, bigger than the mountains.

zenzi.name: Zenzi
zenzi.origin: Zenzi was a Nigandan woman with the ability to enhance and bring to light people's deepest emotions. When she was about to be killed by the troops of the late Erik Killmonger in the edge of a mass grave, she managed to affect her would-be executors and make them kill each other. thumb|left|Zenzi empathically manipulating Wakandans Zenzi became the leader of the Nigandan Army, and allied herself with Tetu, the head of the Wakandan rebel movement known as the People, and used her abilities to incite riots. The Black Panther tracked her down two times. The first time, in the Nigandan Border Region, Zenzi made her escape while the Black Panther fell prey to her abilities. The second time, Black Panther and his Hatut Zeraze ambushed Zenzi, Tetu and several Nigandan soldiers in Southwest Wakanda. During the scuffle, Black Panther knocked out Zenzi, causing her to slip into a coma. Tetu retreated with her and managed to wake her up several days later. Zenzi helped Tetu establish friendly terms with a coexisting rebel force, the Dora Milaje, by using her powers to thwart an attack of Black Panther's Hatut Zeraze. Zenzi later used her abilities to empower the members of the Nigandian Army and have them march towards the Golden City in their final act to overthrow Black Panther. When the People approached the Golden City, Black Panther had old scholar Changamire speak out against Tetu and broadcast it through the Kimoyo Beads. His speech moved countless members of the People's army, which in turn caused the effect of freeing them from Zenzi's grasp. Tetu had her use those few who remained on their side to murder the would-be defectors. She then empowered the remaining soldiers, turning them into mindless brutes that managed to break into the Golden City. Zenzi remained behind the People's forces, so she was not captured when Tetu and his soldiers fell at the hands of Black Panther and his allies, and instead observed from a distance as her enterprise collapsed. Zenzi retreated towards the wilderness through Birnin Zana and met up with two of the People's allies, Zeke Stane and Vanisher, and teleported away with them. Zenzi later joined forces with Doctor Faustus and helped him and Baron Zemo take control of the minds of Wakanda's soldiers so Hydra could force Black Panther to hand over the Cosmic Cube fragment he had hidden away. Zenzi was later recruited by Bast to help the weakened goddess retake her power, which had been stolen by Emperor N'Jadaka, and after doing so became the goddess' new host.

zephyr.name: Zephyr
zephyr.origin: ===Origin=== Zephyr was working as a wench in a tavern in an undisclosed location when she was recruited by the Elementals to become their resident air elemental. The Elementals were supposedly cast out of their own universe millennia ago, arriving on Earth before Atlantis was even built. Using their mastery of the elements, these four beings created a kingdom that was unopposed. Together, the Elementals ruled Earth, millennia before the Asgardians did. At the time, Zephyr's only concern was power. Eventually, the Elementals tried to extend their rule into the land that would be known as Egypt. There, a young warrior named Dann and a wizard named Garrett joined their two souls to arcane magics and created the Ruby Scarab. In the hands of Dann, this magical item sapped the powers of the Elementals and banished them to another universe. From the, Zephyr's only desire was to regain her lost power. ===Search for the Ruby Scarab=== A thousand years ago, searching for the Ruby Scarab to restore her pantheon, Zephyr heard of Thor possessing a ruby artifact. Acting as a wench, she approached him, only to discover the artifact was simply a Seduction Gem. She stole it anyway, for the sake of it. Their confrontation led them to a short but Earth-shattering passion. ===Quitting the Elementals=== When her plan to use the Living Mummy to obtain the Ruby Scarab failed, the other three Elementals expelled her from their ranks. She then joined forces with the adventurers Olddann and the Asp, as well as Alexi Skarab, in defeating her former partners the Elementals. Zephyr later resurfaced on Earth in Saracen Cay, alongside Olddann and the Asp, but her former allies attacked them. They were captured by the Elementals, and she was tortured, to force the others to reveal the location of the Ruby Scarab. After the Elementals finally returned, Zephyr realized that her want for power was dangerous, and left the Elementals after fighting against them. ===Collector=== Zephyr later tried to serve more noble purposes. Unfortunately, Taneleer Tivan, the Collector, who had already captured the other Elementals, trapped her. However, she joined forces with him, as he fell in love with her. She appeared (as something close to an astral form) to Thor during a massive storm. Soon afterwards, when Thor came to alarm the Collector about the arrival of Ego, the Collector showed Thor that he held its brother Alter Ego as part of his collection in his Gallery of Dodecahedra (within a pocket universe). Zephyr had him trapped there to sustain the living planet. Witnessing Thor's escape, his liberation of Alter Ego and refusing to allow either it or its brother Ego to die in a fratricidal fight (Alter Ego wanting to preserve its uniqueness), Zephyr soon recalled what it was like to be driven by an ideal, and deserted Tivan's side to save Thor who had been trapped (on purpose) on Alter Ego's surface trying to stop it, but both of them ended up trapped in the Living Planet's mouth. There, Thor exposed her to his plan of letting himself get swallowed, in order to knock both Alter Ego (and Ego) unconscious from an internal blow. Attacking Alter Ego's core, both gods were blasted. They were thrown into an hallucination while Alter Ego gained sustenance from their energies. Causing a storm in their hallucination, Zephyr was expelled from Alter Ego only to discover a paranoid Collector who was consumed with jealousy of her interactions with Thor, and who then threw her into another Dodecahedron containing a black hole. She was sent six hundred years in the past at the other side of the universe. During that six hundred year-long journey to rejoin Thor, she had many adventures and became closer to Thor's values. As Thor managed to calm Alter Ego (only for it to be almost destroyed in self-defense by Ego), she returned, offering Ego her assistance, and helped recreate Alter Ego as its moon.

zephyr zog.name: Zephyr Zog
zephyr zog.origin: Zephyr Zog was a famous German astrophysicist and string theorist who first learned how to breach the barriers between realities. It was for this reason that the Nazis of Earth-12591 did not turn Zog into a zombie, they needed his motor neurons not to be decomposed so that he could build a trans-dimensional battleship for the Nazi zombies to use in order to spread their infection across the Multiverse. When Zog realized the horrific destruction that the zombies planned to spread across countless universes, he informed A.R.M.O.R. on Earth-616, sending them video footage of the zombies destructive bloodlust. This prompted A.R.M.O.R. to recruit a team of superhumans led by Howard the Duck to go to Earth-12591 and stop the Nazi zombie threat from crossing over into Earth-616's reality. The Ducky Dozen, as the team was known, were led to Zog by this reality's last resistance to the Nazi zombie regime known as the Suffragists. After escaping from Zog's headquarters before being captured by a zombified Dum Dum Dugan, the group boarded Zog's private train and headed towards the Nazi zombies inner sanctum, determined to destroy their trans-dimensional battleship. While travelling to the zombies' headquarters in the Bavarian Alps, Zog and Ducky Dozen member Flexo acted as the train's engineers when they were attacked by a group of zombified Asgardian Valkyrior who were searching for Loki, who had secretly hidden aboard the train. The Valkyrie pinned Flexo to his seat with her spear before killing Zog.

zephyrus jones.name: Zephyrus Jones
zephyrus jones.origin: Zephyr Jones wanted to honor his father Dr. Morrison Jones' hopes of reaching the planet Mars by completing his father's rocket project after his death. Accompanied by his friend Corky Grogan, he would launch his rocket into space. Along the way however, their instruments would malfunction and instead they would be forced to land on the previous unknown planet of Sunev. They would be welcomed by the ruling Birdmen learning that the planet used to be part of Earth. After meeting with King Bolo, Zephyr and Corky would exchange knowledge and Zephyr would fall in love with Princess Tonka. The jealous General Roudo, seeking to turn over the Birdmen's longevity elixir to the evil Parrotmen would frame Zephyr and Corky as spies and the two would be locked up to await execution. When the Parrotmen would attack the Bird-People, Princess Tonka would bring Zephyr and Corky their guns and help free them. The duo would then fight off the Parrotmen and capture Roudo, exposing him as the true spy. After Roudo was executed, Zephyr would teach the Birdmen how to make guns and return home to Earth with Corky, to plan a second mission to Mars. Zephyr's second attempt to fly to Mars would also get sidetracked when Regean Lexico and his daughter Tesi would stow away on his ship and force them to redirect their rocket to the star known as Cygni. Learning that Lexico sought "Star Dust" a replacement for Radium as a fuel source, Zephyr would agree to go. Upon their arrival they would be attacked by the dwarfish Cygnians and the Lexico's would be captured. Zephyr and Corky would come to their rescue, freeing them and burying their Cygnian attackers under tons of rock. Collecting 50 pounds of "Star Dust" to return to Earth, they would head for home. Zephyr Jones has not been seen or heard from since, his fate remains unrevealed.

zerhu.name: Zerhu
zerhu.origin: Not much is known about the past of the man called Zerhu. In 1945 he took leadership of a religious order called the Zurashnu that worshiped the goddess Vurashnu. He had claimed that he was Vurashnu's son and convinced his followers to turn over their valuables to Vurashnu as a sacrificial offering. Unknown to his followers, Zerhu took the possessions for his own material wealth. When one of their members refused to give up his valuables, Zerhu had him killed and when his daughter rebelled he sent his people to eliminate her as well. Their attempt to kill the girl was interrupted by the Angel who managed to convince Zerhu to let the girl go. Learning of the goings on within the group, the Angel agreed to help the woman expose Zerhu as a fraud. They were captured by Zehru and his men to be tortured, but both managed to break free. Being chased to the shrine to Vurashnu, the Angel kept the followers at bay until the woman found the stash of stolen jewels and valuables. Showing them to her fellow believers convinced them of Zehru's double crossing and his former followers then killed him in retribution in such a way it even unnerved the Angel.

zero kurarkill.name: Zero (Kurarkill)
zero kurarkill.origin: thumb|left|Before being transformed Zero was an unnamed former assistant of Dr. Kurarkill. When Kurarkill began experimenting on human and apes to create super intelligent apes at the cost of turning the humans into animals, Zero strongly disagreed with what Kurarkill was doing. In response, Kurarkill turned her into a cat and she somehow escaped and was adopted by Keith and Carrie who gave her the name Zero. When Keith, Carrie, and Iron Man became captives of Dr. Kurarkill and imprisoned in an electrical field, Zero generated sufficient static to disrupt the field, freeing the prisoners. Later, Zero chewed through some of the wires to the gate to Neo-Apes, causing a short that opened the wrong door and the apes seemingly killed the doctor. Zero's fate after this is currently unknown and is presumably still a cat since no one else knew of her transformation.

zet krill.name: Zet Krill
zet krill.species: Alien infected and turned into a Brood
zet krill.origin: Zet Krill was from an alien race from an unidentified planet. He and his parents went out to explore the galaxy in search of new planets to colonize. During their travels they encountered a distress signal and went to investigate. They discovered the signal was a trap by a Brood-Infested Acanti, and attempted to flee but their vessel was boarded. Zet, his sibling and mother were infected and transformed into Brood, his father Tyrus was similarly infected but was able to inject himself with a depressant which suppressed the infection. Ulara then left in the escape pod. Eventually Zet and her brood nest took root on Earth in the Hotel Ripley on Earth, bringing them up against Wolverine and a vengeful Tyrus. After they managed to take out all the Brood, Krill left himself transform into a Brood, tricking Wolverine into killing him. As Krill lay dying he revealed the full truth to Wolverine, who laid Krill with his dying family. Wolverine returned their bodies to the ship and with Beast's help they returned the ship to their homeworld.

zetora.name: Zetora
zetora.origin: thumb|switching body with John Warren (Earth-616)|John Warren Zetora committed a crime on Mars, and was forced to flee to Earth to escape the Martian police. Here he exchanged bodies with John Warren in order to elude the Martian police. When Warren arrived in town he tried to convince people that a Martian inhabited his body. The militia arrived, and they were prepared to shoot Warren, when Warren's dog Spot suddenly attacked Zetora. The militia realized that Zetora was an imposter, and forced him to give Warren his body back. Zetora was taken away by the authorities. He planned to earn a pardon on Mars by conquering Earth. He escaped his cell and clashed with the military, rampaging through New York until arriving at the U.N. building. The U.N. handed over control of the planet to Zetora. He was about to summon an invasion fleet from Mars when he abruptly died. It was later revealed that he was killed by Earth's bacteria, which he had no resistance to. Zetora later turned up alive.

zeus.name: Zeus
zeus.origin: ===Origin=== left|thumb|Zeus in his childhood Born ten of thousands years ago, Zeus was the youngest son of the Titans Cronus, who ruled Olympus, and Rhea. The Titans were the offspring of the sky god Ouranos and the primeval earth goddess Gaea. Cronus overthrew his father's rule by fatally wounding him. The dying Ouranus prophesied that Cronus would likewise be overthrown by one of his own children. As a result, upon the birth of each of his own children, Cronus had the infant imprisoned in Tartarus, the most dismal section of the extra dimensional underworld known as Hades. The offspring he sent there were Hades, Poseidon, Hera, Demeter, and Hestia. Appalled at the mistreatment of their children, Cronus's wife Rhea concealed her sixth pregnancy from him and secretly gave birth to Zeus on Mount Lycaeum in Arcadia, an area of the land now known as Greece. Rhea gave the infant Zeus to the safekeeping of Gaea who hid him on the island of Crete. Seeing that Zeus would not gain the wisdom needed to act as her mercy, she used the Utgard-Key to mark him with Toranos' wheel so he could serve as a lesson for the one who would. ===Titanomachy=== Zeus grew to adulthood among the shepherds of Mount Ida, Crete, and then set about taking revenge on Cronus. Zeus went down into Tartarus and freed his siblings, who had all now grown to adulthood, Zeus also freed the three one-eyed giants called Cyclopes and the three hundred-handed giants called Hekatonchieres, all six of whom Cronus had imprisoned there for fear they would help overthrow him. The grateful Cyclopes taught Zeus how to wield his energy-manipulating powers in battle.250px|left|thumb|"Titanomachy" Zeus and his allies fought a ten-year war with the Titans which ended with Zeus's victory. He imprisoned most of the male Titans in Tartarus and established himself in the small "pocket" dimension of Olympus as supreme ruler of the Olympian race. ===Offspring=== Zeus married the goddess Hera, but he engaged in many affairs with goddesses, titans, nymphs and mortal women and produced various famous offspring. By Hera, he sired Ares, Eris, Hebe, and Hephaestus. His first lover was Metis, a Titan. With her, he sired Athena. A relationship with Dione, a Titan, produced Aphrodite. He was involved with Leto and sired the twins; Apollo and Artemis. He was also involved with Maia, a nymph, and sired Hermes. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Circa 50,000 B.C., the inhabitants of Atlantis seemingly worshiped Jupiter. ===Hyborian Age=== For some reasons, Alexander of Macedon and his armies were briefly sent to the Hyborian Age, 10,000 years before their era, and the descendants of those who stayed there invoked "Zoos", a god unknown to Conan. Around 8000 BC, at the end of the Hyborian Age, beings known as the Olympians traveled from the interdimensional realm of Olympus via a nexus located on Mount Olympus to Earth. They began interacting with the Humans of the region who began to worship them. ===Ancient Greece=== Zeus engaged in many love affairs with mortal women and goddesses, including the wife of Ixion, Danaë, the daughter of Phoenix, Semele, Demeter, Leto, and sired many offspring: Zeus had an affair with Semele, the daughter of King Cadmus of Thebes, who impregnated her and sworn to grant her her every wish. Tricked by Zeus' jealous wife Hera, she asked Zeus to reveal himself to her in all his glory and perished. Her son Dionysus was born there, rescued by Hermes at the behest of Zeus. He eventually reunited with his father atop Mount Olympus. He was the lover of Libyan queen Lamia, whom Hera cursed into becoming a snake-woman that stole children to drink her blood. He sired a mortal son, Sarpedon, a Lycian who fought and died for Troy during the Trojan War. Zeus became infatuated with Alcmena wife of Amphitryon, king of Thebes, Greece. He seduced her by taking the form of her husband. She gave birth to Hercules. It was revealed he created him to be the champion of mankind. ===Eternals=== Zeus also learned that Greece's Mount Olympus, the location of the main inter-dimensional nexus between the Olympian dimension and Earth, lay near Olympia, the principal city of the Eternals. Zeus and his daughter Athena, goddess of wisdom, held a meeting with Zuras, the leader of the Eternals, and his daughter Thena. Noticing the strong physical resemblance between Zeus and Zuras and between Azura and herself, Athena suggested that the Olympian gods and the Eternals form an alliance whereby the Eternals would act as the gods' representatives on Earth. The other three enthusiastically agreed, and Azura took her current name of Thena to signify the signing of the pact. However, over the years many ordinary human beings came to think of many Eternals not as the gods' representatives but as the gods themselves. This led to a growing resentment by the gods towards the Eternals which recently erupted into a brief war. ===Roman Empire=== In 146 B.C., the Romans conquered Macedonia and then Greece. T

zeus panhellenios.name: Zeus Panhellenios
zeus panhellenios.origin: ===Origin=== left|thumb|Zeus in his childhood Born ten of thousands years ago, Zeus was the youngest son of the Titans Cronus, who ruled Olympus, and Rhea. The Titans were the offspring of the sky god Ouranos and the primeval earth goddess Gaea. Cronus overthrew his father's rule by fatally wounding him. The dying Ouranus prophesied that Cronus would likewise be overthrown by one of his own children. As a result, upon the birth of each of his own children, Cronus had the infant imprisoned in Tartarus, the most dismal section of the extra dimensional underworld known as Hades. The offspring he sent there were Hades, Poseidon, Hera, Demeter, and Hestia. Appalled at the mistreatment of their children, Cronus's wife Rhea concealed her sixth pregnancy from him and secretly gave birth to Zeus on Mount Lycaeum in Arcadia, an area of the land now known as Greece. Rhea gave the infant Zeus to the safekeeping of Gaea who hid him on the island of Crete. Seeing that Zeus would not gain the wisdom needed to act as her mercy, she used the Utgard-Key to mark him with Toranos' wheel so he could serve as a lesson for the one who would. ===Titanomachy=== Zeus grew to adulthood among the shepherds of Mount Ida, Crete, and then set about taking revenge on Cronus. Zeus went down into Tartarus and freed his siblings, who had all now grown to adulthood, Zeus also freed the three one-eyed giants called Cyclopes and the three hundred-handed giants called Hekatonchieres, all six of whom Cronus had imprisoned there for fear they would help overthrow him. The grateful Cyclopes taught Zeus how to wield his energy-manipulating powers in battle.250px|left|thumb|"Titanomachy" Zeus and his allies fought a ten-year war with the Titans which ended with Zeus's victory. He imprisoned most of the male Titans in Tartarus and established himself in the small "pocket" dimension of Olympus as supreme ruler of the Olympian race. ===Offspring=== Zeus married the goddess Hera, but he engaged in many affairs with goddesses, titans, nymphs and mortal women and produced various famous offspring. By Hera, he sired Ares, Eris, Hebe, and Hephaestus. His first lover was Metis, a Titan. With her, he sired Athena. A relationship with Dione, a Titan, produced Aphrodite. He was involved with Leto and sired the twins; Apollo and Artemis. He was also involved with Maia, a nymph, and sired Hermes. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Circa 50,000 B.C., the inhabitants of Atlantis seemingly worshiped Jupiter. ===Hyborian Age=== For some reasons, Alexander of Macedon and his armies were briefly sent to the Hyborian Age, 10,000 years before their era, and the descendants of those who stayed there invoked "Zoos", a god unknown to Conan. Around 8000 BC, at the end of the Hyborian Age, beings known as the Olympians traveled from the interdimensional realm of Olympus via a nexus located on Mount Olympus to Earth. They began interacting with the Humans of the region who began to worship them. ===Ancient Greece=== Zeus engaged in many love affairs with mortal women and goddesses, including the wife of Ixion, Danaë, the daughter of Phoenix, Semele, Demeter, Leto, and sired many offspring: Zeus had an affair with Semele, the daughter of King Cadmus of Thebes, who impregnated her and sworn to grant her her every wish. Tricked by Zeus' jealous wife Hera, she asked Zeus to reveal himself to her in all his glory and perished. Her son Dionysus was born there, rescued by Hermes at the behest of Zeus. He eventually reunited with his father atop Mount Olympus. He was the lover of Libyan queen Lamia, whom Hera cursed into becoming a snake-woman that stole children to drink her blood. He sired a mortal son, Sarpedon, a Lycian who fought and died for Troy during the Trojan War. Zeus became infatuated with Alcmena wife of Amphitryon, king of Thebes, Greece. He seduced her by taking the form of her husband. She gave birth to Hercules. It was revealed he created him to be the champion of mankind. ===Eternals=== Zeus also learned that Greece's Mount Olympus, the location of the main inter-dimensional nexus between the Olympian dimension and Earth, lay near Olympia, the principal city of the Eternals. Zeus and his daughter Athena, goddess of wisdom, held a meeting with Zuras, the leader of the Eternals, and his daughter Thena. Noticing the strong physical resemblance between Zeus and Zuras and between Azura and herself, Athena suggested that the Olympian gods and the Eternals form an alliance whereby the Eternals would act as the gods' representatives on Earth. The other three enthusiastically agreed, and Azura took her current name of Thena to signify the signing of the pact. However, over the years many ordinary human beings came to think of many Eternals not as the gods' representatives but as the gods themselves. This led to a growing resentment by the gods towards the Eternals which recently erupted into a brief war. ===Roman Empire=== In 146 B.C., the Romans conquered Macedonia and then Greece. T

zey rogg.name: Zey-Rogg
zey rogg.origin: Like many aliens for a while, Zey-Rogg and his sister, Una-Rogg, wound up on Earth as part of their sentence, and they coincidentally encountered Genis-Vell, the son of the man they thought had killed their father, Yon-Rogg. While Una fought with Marlo Chandler, Zey-Rogg faced Genis, and their fight last for a while, as the two revealed to be each other's equal. In the end, in a split second decision, Genis transported both himself and Zey-Rogg into the Microverse, which resulted in Zey-Rogg ending up on the wrong end of a firing squad meant for Rick Jones.

zgorian.name: Zgorian
zgorian.origin: Exiled to one of the worlds Hulk was sent to when he was trapped at the Crossroads. After showing Hulk the food there was edible, the two became close friends even if the Hulk couldn't understand what Zgorian was saying. After being buried under a rock slide, Zgorian's people returned to pass the death sentence on him for the crime of "showing compassion to the enemy". They subdued the Hulk before killing Zgorian and leaving. This saddened the Hulk and, due to the nature of the spell that had put him in the crossroads, his sadness returned him, leaving Zgorian's body on the desolate world.

zgreb.name: Zgreb
zgreb.species: Celestial turned into a Dark Celestial by the Horde
zgreb.origin: Zgreb is a Celestial who may or may not have originated during the time of the First Cosmos; however, what is known is that Celestials' counterparts across the Multiverse are interconnected aspects of themselves and not separate beings. Thus, the Zgreb of Earth-616 is one aspect of the true Zgreb. ===Earth-616=== Zgreb the Aspirant was a Celestial that came to Earth a million years ago in search of his fellow Celestial, the Progenitor. Upon finding the Progenitor, the Fallen became inflicted with the same Horde that affected it, causing him to become deranged. He was eventually defeated by the Avengers of the Stone Age and buried deep underground in what would become the modern-day country of South Africa, bound by powerful spells. In modern times, a team of archaeologists uncovered the underground cavern where Zgreb had been sealed into, leading to their deaths at the hands of the Celestial. Later, Loki, the Asgardian God of Mischief, released Zgreb from his prison and used him bring about the Final Host of Dark Celestials, so that a threat of their magnitude would reassemble the modern-day Avengers. Some of Earth's heroes attempted to fend off the invaders to no avail. Captain America used Alpha Flight's Omega-Level Warp Grenades to teleport the Dark Celestials to the Sun in an an attempt to destroy them, but it failed. They returned to Earth and traveled to the North Pole, where Loki showed Captain America the corpse of the Progenitor, a Celestial infected by the Horde who had fallen on Earth four billion years into the past. In the meantime, the Dark Celestials started bringing about the Earth's end, causing the ocean to boil and setting the air on fire. The Ghost Rider tracked down the Dark Celestials. He rescued Captain America and abducted Loki, prompting the Dark Celestials to chase after them. All of the heroes convened in Sweden shortly afterwards. Black Panther and Captain Marvel charged themselves with the same energy as the Horde, which allowed them go toe-to-toe against the insects. She-Hulk and Thor harnessed the power of the Blood of Ymir they had retrieved from Asgard. Ghost Rider used his powers to take hold of a dead Celestial's armor. Finally, Iron Man suited up on the Godkiller Armor MK II. Despite their combined strength, the Avengers failed to overpower the Dark Celestials, and in the middle of the battle, the Horde revived the bodies of the Celestials they had infected and felled. After learning of the connection between the Progenitor's death, the Horde and the genetic makeup of humankind, Iron Man rallied the Avengers to join their energies to form a Uni-Mind, since he had been passed on the secrets on how to summon it by Ikaris while investigating the Dark Celestials' arrival. Using the Ghost Rider as a conduit for the Uni-Mind, the Avengers rendered the Horde dormant, reviving the zombified Celestials. The Avengers and the Celestials combined their forces and defeated the Dark Celestials. The Dark Celestials were subsequently apprehended by the Celestials and teleported away from Earth.

zhang heng.name: Zhang Heng
zhang heng.origin: Zhang Heng was born in China's Eastern Han Dynasty, in Luoyang, circa 78 AD. He was the grandchild of Zhang Kan. He studied to be a writer and became a famous poet. At 30, he turned his attention to astronomy. As an inventor, he invented the first seismograph (capable of detecting earthquakes thousands miles away), the first odometer (allowing for the production of accurate maps) and a water-powered armillary sphere. He used that last invention to create the most accurate star map of his era. His genius eventually caught the attention of the , and Zhang Heng was appointed as the Emperor's chief astronomer. As such, his observation assisted in reconfiguring the Chinese calendar. His uncompromising stances prevented him from rising in the court's ranks. At some point, he became the holder of the Spear of Imhotep, an artifact fated to reside in the East, while the Shield of Imhotep remained in the West, in the Brotherhood of the Shield. thumb|left|With the Celestial Madonna In 114 AD, in his palace of Luoyang, he met with a Celestial mother. Before addressing her, he had given the Spear to his disciple, asking him to slay the Celestial if the talk failed. The Space Goddess informed him of the Celestial Egg implanted within Earth, to which Zhang replied that it would not be disturbed, and that she carried herself an unborn Celestial. She then asked him to choice if the nourishment/energy she needed to proceed the delivery should come from the destruction of Earth or of the Moon. Zhang instead suggested that the gestation would occur within the Sun. Zhang Heng then stepped down due to political intrigues with the court's eunuchs under . He later served as administrator of the city of Hejian, and briefly returned to the Emperor's court before his death in 139 AD. The Celestial in the Sun was detected by Lorenzo in 1495. The Star Child was later born and then recovered by Leonardo da Vinci in 1956.

fields.notes: Zhang Heng is sometimes stated to be a member of the Brotherhood of the Shield, and there is a statue of him in the Brotherhood of the Shield's base in Florence, but he holds the Spear, not the Shield. Logically, he should instead be a member of the Brotherhood of the Spear, before its corruption. His profile in does not list him as a member of the Brotherhood of the Shield. Regardless, the Shield in the West and the Spear in the East were very close back then and they were originally one greater brotherhood to begin with, before they drifted apart.

zhao tang.name: Zhao Tang
zhao tang.origin: ===China Force=== At an early age, after each manifesting mutant powers, twins Zhao and Jhimon Tang were selected by the Chinese Communist government for training in the use of their mutants abilities . Upon completion of their training, both siblings were to join China's government-sponsored super team, officially dubbed China Force. The team was to function as an internal line of Chinese defense, as well as an answer the perceived threats of the government sponsored teams in the United States, the Soviet Union, and others. ===Hong Kong Scheme=== However, under as yet unreported circumstances, China Force was splintered by several defections, sparking Zhao and Jhimon (also called Auric and Silver, respectively) to also flee the country, into then-British Hong Kong. In Hong Kong, Silver and Auric became involved in an attempt to overthrow the government to prevent the planned absorption of Hong Kong to China. That scheme was thwarted partly due to the efforts of freelance international intelligence agent Rick Mason. ===Gamma Flight=== Silver and Auric defected to Canada, calling themselves Zhao and Jhimon Tang. The Canadian government offered them citizenship in exchange for working with Gamma Flight II, led by the second Nemesis. The twins, with the rest of Gamma Flight, fought their predecessors, Alpha Flight, although this was part of a plan by the evil Llan the Sorcerer. Once free of the Sorcerer's influence, Nemesis' Gamma Flight soon disbanded by the government in order to re-sanction Alpha Flight. Silver and Auric joined the newly created Beta Flight. ===Auctioned Off=== Shortly after joining Beta Flight, the two were kidnapped by the Sphinx, and they both died while being experimented on. The villain team known as the Chess Set hoped to auction the power-filled corpses of Silver and Auric, inviting criminals of all types to the Sphinx's base. The auction was interrupted by the hero team The New Warriors and Spider-Man, and the Sphinx's base was destroyed. In the resulting explosion, the corpses of the siblings merged with a scientist investigating the site, creating a unique, Category:Gestalt Charactersseparate energy being consisting the merged consciousness of Silver, Auric, and the scientist. The being left for space and its subsequent activities remain unrevealed.

zhao yen.name: Zhao Yen
zhao yen.species: Human mortal having achieved godhood as a Xian upon eating P'an-t'ao, the Peaches of Immortality.
zhao yen.origin: ===Youth=== Zhao Yen was born a frail sickly child in the 4th century BC in the State of Wei (near modern-day Kaifeng, China), and was destined to die before his twenties. However, a fortune teller told him to travel to a nearby field with food and rice wine. There, he encountered two elderly men playing a game of strategy. Thankful for his hospitality, they revealed themselves as the gods in Yu Huang's service who were responsible for fixing the birth and death dates of mortals, and granted him immortality and godhood upon eating P'an-t'ao, the Peaches of Immortality. ===God of health and longevity=== ====Early years==== Becoming Shou-Hsing (壽星), the Taoist God (or Xian) of health and longevity, he inherited the responsibility of assigning the life span of mortals. He became also affiliated with Fu-Hsing, god of good fortune and Lu-Hsing, god of prosperity, and was later promoted as the official vizier to Yu Huang within the Jade Court at Yujing Shan. ====Modern days==== ...

zharkah.name: Zharkah
zharkah.origin: Zharkah was born in a planet governed by a strict caste system resulting from the interference of the Celestials. The Chosen were those gifted with magnificent abilities but no physical deviance, while the Rejects displayed phenotypical differences among themselves. As a Reject, Zharkah knew nothing but violence and disdain from the ruling class of Chosen, who saw her people as invalid and inferior creatures. In constant war with her opponents, she became a valuable leadership figure of the Djade tribe. Tragically, she saw many of her offspring not survive birth. When the group of alien mutants known as X-Factor were dragged onto her planet as a result of the machinations of the Celestials, Zharkah met Beast, who she believed to be one of the Rejects. X-Factor was separated due to the intervention of the Celestial Gammenon and Beast joined the Rejects in their city. Having developed a strong connection with Beast, Zharkah was shocked to learn about the different members of X-Factor. Despite displaying loyalty, she was unable to reveal to her new ally she kept his teammate Jean Grey captive. Zharkah specifically kept the information to test if Beast was a Reject or not. Upon finding Jean Grey being transported, he attempted to free her, prompting Zharkah to judge him as a traitorous infiltrator. Beast was caged, but managed to escape. As he attempted to escape, it was revealed to Zharkah that Beast came from another planet, thus not being either a Reject or a Chosen. Knowing Beast's true intentions, Zharkah and the Djade tribe supported him in his quest to reunite X-Factor. Zharkah led the Rejects into the citadel of the Chosen to end their ruthless and corrupted rule, implemented by the vile Palik. As the Celestials judged and threatened the planet, Zharkah decided to have the Rejects join the Chosen, X-Factor and all other factions to protect their existence. She made the difficult decision to embrace change and different ideologies to prosper in battle. This caused the Celestials to leave the planet and a united community was able to thrive in peace.

zheng shang chi.name: Zheng Shang-Chi
zheng shang chi.species: Human;; Shang was raised to become a deadly assassin by his father, the immortal crimelord and sorcerer Zheng Zu.
zheng shang chi.origin: ===Early Life=== thumb|right|Master of Kung Fu Shang was raised to become a deadly assassin by his father, the immortal crime lord and sorcerer Fu Manchu. However, Shang-Chi became aware of his father's evil nature and defected after his first assignment. He then began to attack various elements of his father's criminal empire and allied himself with his father's archenemy, Denis Nayland Smith, and MI-6. In retaliation, Fu Manchu sent a number of assassins to kill him. His travels led him to meet a number of other martial artists and super heroes around the world: he met his rival, Cat; and teamed up with Iron Fist, Jack of Hearts, and White Tiger to take down the Corporation. After years of playing at "games of deceit and death", Shang-Chi retired from the espionage world. He resurfaced to assist his old friends from MI-6 against the Si-Fan ninjas. Over a decade later, his sister Fah Lo Suee, now called Cursed Lotus was once again involved in the criminal underworld. Fah Lo Suee headed a narcotics empire supplying the highly addictive drug, Wild Tiger. Representing her in Hong Kong was the Wild Tiger Mob led by Deng Ling-Xiao. It was brought down by Shang-Chi who never learned that she was behind it all. fields.personality: Originally portrayed as a stoic and emotionally detached martial artist, Shang-Chi gradually developed into a more relatable and personable hero while retaining his discipline, humility, and commitment to inner peace. Although devoted to meditation and self-improvement, he has always sought a simple, ordinary life free from violence. Throughout much of his career, however, Shang-Chi repeatedly found himself drawn back into the "games of death and deceit" surrounding his father's criminal empire, despite his constant efforts to escape them. Even after forging a new life in San Francisco, he continued to struggle with balancing domestic normalcy against the responsibilities of his family legacy. During his years working alongside MI-6 and later Freelance Restorations, Shang-Chi often questioned whether he was truly serving justice or merely being used as a weapon against his father. Although he formed close friendships with many of his allies, he occasionally endured prejudice and racial stereotyping from some of them. Rather than remaining silent, Shang-Chi openly challenged such attitudes, refusing to allow either his heritage or his father's reputation to define him. After assuming leadership of the Five Weapons Society following the fall of Zheng Zu, Shang-Chi dedicated himself to reforming the organization into a force for good. While he accepted the role out of duty rather than ambition, he frequently felt caught between two worlds, viewed with suspicion by fellow superheroes because of his position while simultaneously facing skepticism from members of the Society who questioned his compassionate leadership. Despite his calm demeanor, Shang-Chi possesses a dry, self-aware sense of humor and often comments on the absurdity of his circumstances. He has admitted to deliberately adopting a slower, proverb-like manner of speaking around Westerners, recognizing that it causes people to pay closer attention to his words. Beneath his confidence, Shang-Chi carries an immense sense of responsibility toward his family, sometimes keeping secrets from his allies or making idealistic decisions to protect his siblings, even at his own expense. His greatest fear is becoming like his father, and moments in which he has been corrupted by dark influences have only strengthened his resolve to define himself by his own choices rather than his bloodline. Shang-Chi's relationships with his siblings further illustrate his role as both their leader and moral compass. While each possesses contrasting personalities and philosophies, he consistently strives to guide them toward redemption rather than domination. Esme's sarcastic wit and willingness to employ lethal force frequently clash with Shang-Chi's pacifism, whereas Takeshi enthusiastically supports his leadership despite his impulsive nature. Although Shi-Hua initially resented Shang-Chi and sought to surpass him, she ultimately abandoned her vendetta after recognizing his genuine devotion to their family. Zhilan, whose quiet integrity and desire for peace closely mirror Shang-Chi's own ideals, became one of his closest allies after realizing they shared the same commitment to justice over power.

fields.trivia: Although Shang-Chi was a uniquely Marvel Comics creation, many of his supporting cast members including Fu Manchu, Fah Lo Suee, and Sir Denis Nayland Smith were actually the creation of early 20th century novelist . Fu Manchu and Denis Nayland Smith made their literary debuts in the 1916 novel The Insidious Dr. Fu Manchu. In 1995, Marvel Comics almost outsourced the production of a line of four interconnected series to Milestone Media. Shang-Chi was going to star one of these books. The pitch of the story, written by Dwayne McDuffie, consisted of Shang-Chi traveling around the globe to dismantle his father's criminal empire and also adding firearms to his combat repertoire. The entire project fell apart since McDuffie had arranged it with Tom DeFalco and Mark Gruenwald. DeFalco would be soon replaced as Editor-in-Chief, and Gruenwald would pass away a year later. Shang-ChiBuddhist identifies himself as a 'bodhisattva', a 'person who is on the path towards Buddhahood but has not yet attained it.' The name Shang-Chi was created by Steve Englehart, through his study of the I-Ching, combining the characters 升 (shēng, “to ascend”) and 氣 (qì, “vital energy”), meaning “the rising and advancing of the spirit.” In 2019, actor Ronny Chieng (featured in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings) advised against using the translation 上氣 (shàng qì), which in modern Chinese means something like “upper air” — an odd fit for a superhero. Chieng suggested 神奇 (shén qí, “magical” or “wonderful”) as a more culturally appropriate alternative. To preserve Englehart's original intent, the most accurate translation would be 昇華的靈氣 (shēnghuá de língqì). In (October 2025), Shen Qi was used as the name for the Earth-6160 variant.

zheng yi.name: Zheng Yi
zheng yi.origin: ===Origins=== Zheng Yi and his older brother Zheng Zu were powerful sorcerers born during the 18th century Qing Dynasty in China. The two brothers and their five disciples, the Deadly Warriors, formed the Five Weapons Society to protect China. Through the use of longevity spells, Yi and Zu lived decades beyond their natural lifespans, outliving their original disciples and leaving them old and weak during the Opium Wars in the next century. During a battle with the British Army, the Five Weapons Society suffered a horrible defeat by Dormammu and his Mindless Ones, resulting in the deaths of the then current lineup of Deadly Warriors and Yi receiving mortal wounds. With the Eyes of the Dragon, Zu attempted to revive his brother and restore his youth at the cost of his own life, but Yi reversed the spell due to not wanting the rule the Society alone, sacrificing himself to restore Zu's youth and power. Zu led the Society alone from then, but without his kind hearted brother's influence he became increasingly ruthless and corrupt, transforming the Society into a vast criminal empire. To instill fear, Zu lied about Yi's death, claiming he murdered Yi for his perceived weakness and stole his life energy to augment his own. ===Life Beyond Death=== Zheng Yi appeared to his nephew Shang-Chi as a spirit, urging him to visit his tomb in Henan. At Yi's tomb, Shang-Chi requested his uncle's guidance in stopping his sister Shi-Hua and for a cure for his wound inflicted by the jiangshi created by her. Instead, Yi told his nephew to stop running away from his family and revealed the truth of Zheng Zu's past. Shang-Chi recalled Yi's words while fighting Shi-Hua, which prevented him from being mutated into a jiangshi.

zheng zhilan.name: Zheng Zhilan
zheng zhilan.origin: One of the many daughters of the sorcerer and crimelord Zheng Zu, Zhilan was raised in the House of the Deadly Staff outside of London, England. When Zhilan sought to reform the Five Weapons Society, Zheng Zu ordered Brother Sabre to assassinate her for her insolence. Instead, Brother Sabre spared Zhilan and faked her death. Unbeknownst to the two half-siblings, the real reason why their father ordered Zhilan's death was due to her status as a mutant, a species that Zu believed had the potential to become a dangerous colonial threat. During her exile, Zhilan took up residence in in Ireland, where she used her mutant abilities to assist the locals, earning the reputation as the "Witch of Muckross Lake". Her actions were eventually captured on social media, prompting the new Supreme Commander of the Society and her half-brother Shang-Chi to seek her out. Believing Shang-Chi, Brother Sabre, and Sister Dagger came to kill her, Zhilan attacked them; the fight was interrupted by Wolverine, who revealed Zhilan's existence as a mutant and attempted to bring her to Krakoa for her protection. After a prolonged struggle, Shang-Chi was able to clear up the misunderstanding with Wolverine and Zhilan. Realizing that Shang-Chi had implemented the same reforms that she sought for the Society, Zhilan politely turned down Wolverine's invitation to Krakoa and accepted Shang's offer to rejoin the Society as its new Sister Staff. Wolverine held off a mob of anti-mutant protestors while Zhilan escaped with her half-siblings to the House of the Deadly Hand in New York. While resting in her private quarters, Zhilan was visited by Chieftain Xin, who offered her a proposal. Sister Staff accompanied Shang-Chi and her siblings when they broke into the Baxter Building to gain access to the Negative Zone, casting a mind numbing spell to incapacitate the building's staff and guests and destroyed the H.E.R.B.I.E.s guarding Mister Fantastic's lab with her solidified music. In the Negative Zone, Sister Staff and her siblings met Jiang Li, Shang-Chi's mother, for the first time and brought her back to Earth, where they got into an altercation with the Fantastic Four. Sister Staff briefly fought against Invisible Woman before escaping with her family back to the House of the Deadly Hand. Sister Staff later joined up with several former allies-turned-enemies of the Society, including King Wild Man, Lady Iron Fan and Red Dot, who were recruited by Xin where he revealed his plans to bring an end to Shang-Chi's rule. While at the House of the Deadly Sabre with her siblings, Sister Staff saw Shang-Chi get confronted by several of his superhero allies who demanded he hand over a Cosmic Cube they believed he stole and came to his aid when the confrontation turned violent. While he fought Thor, Shang-Chi realized Brother Sabre had stolen the Cube and lied to him about it, prompting him to hand Takeshi over to the heroes as a prisoner along with the Cube. Zhilan later met with Xin and informed him of the events that had transpired. Zhilan later joined Xin's allies during their assault against Shang-Chi at the New House of the Deadly Hand, revealing to all her betrayal was due to her belief that Shang-Chi cared more about his western allies than his family when he handed Brother Sabre to the Avengers. However, this turned out to be a ruse and Zhilan helped Shang-Chi and the Society defeat the would-be assassins, admitting to Shang-Chi that his actions with Takeshi proved that he held to his principles above all else, earning her trust as leader. Unfortunately, the assassins took Jiang Li hostage, forcing Shang-Chi to release them and regrouping with Xin, taking a portal to Qilin Island. When Shang-Chi agreed with Xin to exchange his life for Jiang Li's, Sister Staff accompanied him and Sister Dagger to the Mauna Kea summit in Hawai'i for the exchange, where Staff promised to care for Jiang Li as her own mother after getting her back. Xin and the Qilin Riders arrived without Jiang Li and attacked the three siblings. When Shang-Chi was able to fight him off, Xin resorted to using some of Shang-Chi's blood to create three taotie before fleeing back to Ta-Lo. Sister Staff and her siblings defeated one taotie and saved Falo from the second one. While researching the taotie, the siblings realized that Xin created them to hunt anyone in Zheng Zu's lineage and that Falo was a descendant of their father. Falo attempted to make a pass at Sister Staff but was threatened by Dagger, revealing that Staff was related to him as his ancestor was her father. Sister Staff traveled with her siblings to the Vault where they saved Takeshi from the third taotie. When Shang-Chi received a vision of Shi-Hua getting attacked by Xin, he freed Brother Sabre from the Vault's guardsmen despite Sister Staff's reminder of staying true to his principles, and the four traveled to British Columbia to rescue Sister Hammer after she was left for dead by Xin. zheng zu.origin: ===Origins=== Zheng Zu and his younger brother, Zheng Yi, were powerful sorcerers born during the 18th century Qing Dynasty in China. The two brothers and their five disciples, the Deadly Warriors, formed the Five Weapons Society to protect China. The structure and naming system of the Five Weapons Society was inspired by the legend of Ta-Lo's Five Sets of Heavenly Weapons, which consisted of the One Hammer (Hammer), Two Swords (Sabre), Three Staffs (Staff), Nine Daggers (Dagger), and Ten Rings (Hand). Through the use of longevity spells, the sorcerer brothers lived decades beyond their natural lifespans, outliving their original disciples and leaving them old and weak during the Opium Wars in the next century. During a battle with the British Army, the Five Weapons Society suffered a horrible defeat by Dormammu and his Mindless Ones, resulting in the deaths of the then-current lineup of Deadly Warriors and Yi receiving mortal wounds. With the Eyes of the Dragon, Zu attempted to revive his brother and restore his youth at the cost of his own life, but Yi reversed the spell due to not wanting to rule the Society alone, sacrificing himself to restore Zu's youth and power. Zu led the Society alone from then, but without his kindhearted brother's influence he became increasingly ruthless and corrupt, transforming the Society into a vast criminal empire. To instill fear, Zu lied about Yi's death, claiming that he murdered Yi for his perceived weakness and stole his life energy to augment his own. Over the years, Zu learned the martial arts, the various scientific disciplines, and esoteric knowledge at a monastery. In the modern day, Zu adopted the name "Dr. Fu Manchu" and created the false origin that he was empowered by the Elixir of Life. As with his name, the Society would go through different aliases over the years, beginning with the Celestial Order of the Si-Fan and, eventually, the Order of the Golden Dawn and the Celestial Order of the Hai-Dai. He became a crimelord, the shadow emperor of a worldwide invisible empire with a globe-spanning army of highly trained fanatical killers. At his command were the killers of various Asian cults and secret societies, including the Dacoits, the Thugees, the Phansigars, the Hashishin, the Jezails, and others. "Dr. Fu Manchu" had the intellect of three geniuses and used the world's most beautiful women as his pawns. ===The 20th Century=== It was during the Boxer Rebellion that Zu led the Five Weapons Society against the invaders, only to learn that the House of the Deadly Sabre had fallen to the foreigners. Zu reprimanded the Deadly Warriors for not properly preparing for such an assault. Commander Sabre begged for forgiveness and mercy for his failure; Zu then let Sabre in on a old secret before decapitating him: Zheng Yi had similarly been weak and, rather than being held back, he murdered his own brother and stole his spirit energy to augment his own. When he realized that China could not remain isolated from the rest of the world forever, he set up bases across the globe, establishing new strongholds in England, Japan, Russia, and France. Zu discovered the existence of a gateway to Ta Lo on Earth and planned to steal the Five Sets of Heavenly Weapons to bolster the Five Weapons Society. Upon arriving at Qilin Island, Zu was betrayed and left for dead by pirates under his service but was rescued by Jiang Li of the Qilin Riders. While being nursed back to health, Zu and Jiang Li fell in love with each other. When Jiang Li's father, Chieftain Xin, discovered Zu's presence on the island, he ordered his daughter to execute the trespasser, but the two fled to the House of the Deadly Hand. When she discovered that Zu led a criminal organization, Jiang Li attempted to leave him, but Zu promised to change his evil ways. The two married and had two children: a son, Shang-Chi, and a daughter, Shi-Hua. Within the first few years into his marriage, Zheng Zu grew to genuinely love his family. However, following an attack by Hydra against the House of the Deadly Hand, Zu became cold and distant towards his family, as he felt that his love for them had made him weak, and resumed his plans to infiltrate Ta Lo. Xin and Jiang Li confronted Zu in his personal tower, where they discovered that he had constructed a makeshift portal to Ta Lo. While Zu fought his wife and father-in-law, Shang-Chi happened upon the scene, just as the portal's connection to Ta Lo became disconnected and Jiang Li was accidentally pushed through, sending her to the Negative Zone. Zu and Xin blamed each other for Jiang Li's presumed death and each tried convincing Shang-Chi to join them. Shang-Chi sided with his father and threw one of Zu's chemicals at Xin's face, blinding him and leaving a scar across his right eye. Xin denounced Shang-Chi to be as evil as his father and fled. Zu subsequently placed a memory spell on Shang-Chi, making him forget the incident. During their childhood, Shang-Chi and Shi-Hua acc

fields.notes: Dr. Fu Manchu was originally created by British pulp novelist (real name: Arthur Henry/Sarsfield Ward) and was the eponymous antagonist in 13 novels, one novella, and three short stories published between 1913 and 1959. Dr. Fu Manchu's greatest adversaries were Sir Denis Nayland Smith and Dr. Petrie (also creations of Rohmer). His famous son, Shang-Chi, is a character who is unique to the Marvel Universe and, therefore, has no pulp era counterpart. As Marvel Comics Entertainment no longer maintains the license to use Dr. Fu Manchu as a character, he is seldom referenced in comics, but does occasionally appear under an assumed name. His daughter, Fah Lo Suee, is also a creation of Rohmer, and is also called by other names. The Marvel Comics version of Dr. Fu Manchu was first developed by Roy Thomas and Steve Englehart. On Earth-616 Dr. Fu Manchu is a real person, but most people believe him to be a fictional character: A poster seen in (1967) depicts this character in a poster with the text "Fu Manchu for Mayor" in the Coffee Bean. These posters were part of a real-life campaign during the to promote the 1965 film . In (1974), Spider-Man believed that Dr. Fu Manchu was a fictional character until they actually met one another - and even then, Spider-Man was still skeptical. In Rohmer's novels, novella, and short stories the Si-Fan, the Dacoits and the Thugees are groups that serve Dr. Fu Manchu; although in real life, the names "Thugees" and "Phansigars" refer to the same group, but in the comics they were portrayed as distinct. The Thugees are recognized as worshipers of the Hindu goddess Kali. This connection is not shown in the comics; however, in , the Cult of Kali is said to be part of Dr. Fu Manchu's organization, the Celestial Order of the Si-Fan. Han is the name of the villain in , starring Bruce Lee; this fact is mentioned by Luke Cage and Han appears on the cover of . A scene from the film, with Bruce Lee and actor Shih Kien (as Han), appears in . Han has been compared to Dr. Fu Manchu. Although the Celetial Order of the Hai-Dai is mentioned in and , the same was not true of Zheng Bao Yu. Apparently, Shi-Hua was created to replace her, as Bao Yu is a version of , the daughter of Dr. Fu Manchu. There is also no mention of other groups like the Phansigars and the Dacoits or even the time when the Kingpin controlled the Si-Fan and implemented Cyber-Ninjas. The Mandarin, the Yellow Claw and Zheng Zu all claim to be descendants of Genghis Khan.

zhered na.origin: ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Zhered-Na was a sorceress from Atlantis during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age, practicing white magic and worshipping Valka (allegedly the son of the Elder Goddess Gaea). ====Assemblage of Avatars (19,000 BC)==== Circa 19,000 BC, as conflicts broke out again between the Elder Gods (Oshtur and Chthon, Set, and Gaea), Agamotto (Oshtur's son, member with her of the Vishanti mystic trinity, and Earth's first "Sorcerer Supreme", though the title wasn't used until thousand years later), summoned to Atlantis the representatives of the four Elder Gods, the greatest sorcerers of the ancient era, the Assemblage of Avatars. Zhered represented Gaea, presumably among several others, including Lady Linnea. Very little was accomplished during the summit (though it became legendary), and Agamotto would soon began to grow frustrated with mankind's limitation. Though, he continued to observe and began to groom Zhered-Na into his successor, impressed by her. ====Great Cataclysm and Death (18,000 BC)==== Circa 18,000 BC, after refusing already twice to cease prophesying the coming Great Cataclysm that would cause Atlantis to sink into the sea, she was exiled to the mainland by Kamuu and Zartra. She was killed by a cultist manipulated by D'Spayre for revenge against her for defeating his master, the Dweller in Darkness. ===Modern Age=== She once assisted Daimon Hellstrom in defeating the demo-snake Kometes.
zhered na.bio: ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Zhered-Na was a sorceress from Atlantis during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age, practicing white magic and worshipping Valka (allegedly the son of the Elder Goddess Gaea). ====Assemblage of Avatars (19,000 BC)==== Circa 19,000 BC, as conflicts broke out again between the Elder Gods (Oshtur and Chthon, Set, and Gaea), Agamotto (Oshtur's son, member with her of the Vishanti mystic trinity, and Earth's first "Sorcerer Supreme", though the title wasn't used until thousand years later), summoned to Atlantis the representatives of the four Elder Gods, the greatest sorcerers of the ancient era, the Assemblage of Avatars. Zhered represented Gaea, presumably among several others, including Lady Linnea. Very little was accomplished during the summit (though it became legendary), and Agamotto would soon began to grow frustrated with mankind's limitation. zhib ran.name: Zhib-Ran
zhib ran.origin: Zhib-Ran was an elected leader of a world called Yttrium in the Microverse which was destroyed until repeated incursions into the Microverse by Genis-Vell battling Sentry unleashed vast energies that disrupted Yttrium's axis, destroying it in the process. Zhib-Ran was the sole survivor of this catastrophe, thrown into a cosmic maelstrom until he was rescued by Grandmaster who brought him to Earth. The incident granted him radiation-based superpowers. After learning about the reasons behind his world's destruction from Grandmaster, he joined the reformed Squadron Sinister and clashed with the Thunderbolts. Aside from his revenge against Genis-Vell, Hyperion's goal was to help protect the Earth, by any means necessary. He was, however, manipulated by the power-seeking Grandmaster to serve in his campaign against Baron Zemo over the control of the access to the Wellspring of Power. During Squadron's final battle against Thunderbolts, Hyperion was defeated by Radioactive Man who was able to suppress his radiation-based powers. Ultimately, he and the rest of the Squadron disappeared without a trace among the unleashed energies of Wellspring of Power, during the fight between Zemo and Grandmaster.

zhilla char.name: Zhilla Char
zhilla char.origin: Not much is known about Zhilla aside from the circumstances leading to her death. Approximately 800 years ago, when wandering the Astral Plane to digest the essence stolen from her victims, she wandered close to Nightmare's realm, attracting his attention. The predator became a victim, as Nightmare forced himself upon her, impregnating her in the process. Nightmare then left her in a lower realm from which she was unable to escape. Succubi mothers are replaced by their children, and so Zhilla's body burned away. In place was left her daughter, who inherited all of her mother's memories.

zhou cheng.name: Zhou Cheng
zhou cheng.origin: Zhou Cheng was a host for the Ch'i-Lin who hunted down and killed many Iron Fists on their 33rd birthday for his master. While it's unknown exactly when he started serving as the Ch'i-Lin's host, his earliest known kill was the Iron Fist Kwai Jun-Fan in 1878 Texas. Despite Zhou's killing of Kwai, the Ch'i-Lin failed to consume Shou-Lao's egg. In 1937, Zhou attempted to hunt down that era's Iron Fist Orson Randall. After being chased throughout the whole world, Randall managed to evade Zhou by injecting himself with heroin to dampen his chi. Over 70 years later, Zhou attacked the current Iron Fist Danny Rand in Central Park and nearly succeeded in killing him, but was forced to flee when Rand called in Luke Cage and the Daughters of the Dragon for backup. Zhou went to the Thunder Dojo to use Rand's students as hostages against him, but Rand anticipated this and summoned the Immortal Weapons for help, forcing him to flee again. The Ch'i-Lin grew impatient and threatened Zhou's life if he failed again, so Zhou made one last attempt to kill Rand by having his lover Nadine, who was working as Rand's secretary, poison Rand to weaken him. Nadine immediately regretted this and pleaded with Zhou stop as she was pregnant with his child, which briefly caught him off guard. Rand managed to fight off Zhou by masking his chi and fighting uncoordinated, which prevented Zhou from predicting his attacks, with help from Cage. When Zhou mocked him, Rand gathered all his anger and punched through his throat, killing him. His body then burned away into a charred skeleton while the Ch'i-Lin left his body. While searching through Zhou's apartment to discover his past, the Immortal Weapons were able to find a map to the Eighth City, which they had been looking for.

zhou man she.name: Zhou Man She
zhou man she.first_appearance: Master of Kung Fu: Bleeding Black Vol 1 1
zhou man she.origin: Zaran, also known as Zhou Man She, is a formidable mercenary and assassin, highly skilled in both armed and unarmed combat. His journey has led him to numerous conflicts with various heroes across the globe, particularly Shang-Chi. Initially trained by Maximillian Zaran, Zhou Man She eventually surpassed his master and assumed the identity of Zaran . He was later hired by Shadow-Hand to recover Fu Manchu’s reliquary, a container believed to hold a map to the Elixir Vitae . This mission put him at odds with Clive Reston and Black Jack Tarr, as well as Shang-Chi . Zaran played a pivotal role during the Burundan civil war, operating under General Bushman as the leader of one of his deadly squads . Later, he was tasked with infiltrating an A.I.M. facility to steal the Z99 chemical agent for Fu Manchu, eliminating multiple operatives in the process . Following this, Fu Manchu ordered Zaran and Dacoits to assassinate Shang-Chi, promising him great rewards. Zaran tracked him down and killed the family Shang-Chi was living with at the time . The two engaged in an intense battle that spanned Canal Street, ending with Zaran’s capture by the police . Despite his imprisonment, Zaran managed to escape using a concealed dart to unlock his restraints . However, his failure to eliminate Shang-Chi displeased Fu Manchu, who sent agents Mr. Lu and Zingh to execute him . Zaran fought back but was eventually subdued. Rather than killing him, Fu Manchu granted him one last chance to complete his mission . Zaran later led an attack on the Marvel Knights headquarters, bringing him into direct combat with Shang-Chi, Moon Knight, and Daredevil . Though he fought fiercely, he was eventually bested by Shang-Chi . In the chaos following an explosion, Zaran attempted to escape but fell from a skyscraper, barely managing to survive . During the events of Secret Wars, Zaran was captured by Emila Vachon and subjected to mind-control technology, forcing him into a docile, repetitive behavioral state under the alias Mr. Muscatel . He was later freed when Misty Knight and Colleen Wing disrupted the control mechanism .

zhu rong.name: Zhu Rong
zhu rong.origin: Zhu Rong (祝融) was the Taoist god (Xian) of fire. Since ancient times, he was tasked with maintaining the cosmic balance by establishing and protecting the boundaries between Heaven and Earth -- a task that brought him into conflict with his son, Gong-Gong. left|300px|thumb|Zhu Rong's humanoid form with tiger In modern times, the android known as The One, believing itself to be Wendell Rand, opened a portal to Feng-Tu in order to resurrect Heather Rand. This apparently upset the cosmic balance, and for retribution, Zhu Rong was summoned to destroy New York City. While wreaking havoc, Iron Fist fused with The One, which was wired to Rand Tower. It was rebuilt into a giant robot and it fought Zhu Rong. However, he was still able to overpower and defeat it. In a last ditch effort, Danny absorbed all the chi from The One, destroying it in the process and jumped out the robot. He used all the chi at once and shot himself through Zhu Rong's head, killing him.

ziigwan.origin: Ziigwan was a student of magic and an intern at Alex Orlok's Orloktek, a company that intended to use magic for commercial purposes. After being saved along with Orlok by Wong when they were trapped in another dimension, it was discovered that it was a trick to be able to use Wong's knowledge to travel in a dimensional plane to be able to exploit the magical powers of an elder god, but after being treated badly by Orlok for the umpteenth time, Ziigwan rebelled against her and helped Wong defeat Orlok. In gratitude Wong granted Ziigwan's will to erase Orlok's memories of the last 5 weeks and furthermore Wong made Ziigwan a helper to him who would deal with requests for help with Doctor Strange's permission.

zimm.name: Zimm
zimm.origin: Zimm was a member of a group of Kamado aliens who supported their Emperor's exiled son, Prince Ch'kra. Ch'kra fell ill on Earth, and the aliens abducted humans in order to harness their bio-energy and heal the Prince. But after capturing Dr. Strange, they were easily defeated by the Defenders summoned by Strange's astral form and rather than being captured, believing that the Defenders were allies of the Emperor, they preferred to commit suicide.

zinn.name: Zinn
zinn.origin: Zinn was one of Salome's slaves. He probably was a normal human. His cranium was deformed and his face was horrible. Zinn was called by Salome after she learned that the battle against the Zuagirs was lost. Zinn followed his master down to the prisons to kill Taramis, but when they reached the corridor where the Taramis' cell was, they found a guard dead. They heard the voices of Conan and Taramis and waited behind a corner. When the liberators reached them, Taramis blinded them with blue flashes and Zinn slew them with his knife. Zinn transported Taramis in the Temple but Conan reached them. Zinn tried to stop Conan but he was easily killed by the Cimmerian.

zip zephyr.name: Zip Zephyr
zip zephyr.origin: Zip Zephyr first appeared after the fallout of Gang War in Brooklyn, challenging the young Spider-Man while he was on patrol with Ms. Marvel and Shift. Zip Zephyr first fires his magical bag of wind currents known as sakkos at Miles which the Spider-Man dodges. While fighting the trio of superheroes Zip Zephyr brags about his demi-god status while ridiculing so called "mortals" like Miles. Though Zephyr possessed great strength and agility he was no match for all three of the young heroes and was quickly debilitated from a monstrous punch from shift, being webbed up by Miles for the local authorities to retrieve him. Zip Zephyr was shown terrorizing the NYPD in hopes of proving he deserves his place in the lineage of the Anemoi, While releasing Destructive air waves strong enough to dismantle swat cars and buildings. Just when Zip Zephyr thought he achieved victory his rival Miles Morales arrived with a vicious kick to the demi-god's face. Zephyr, while frustrated by the young spider's kick and taunts, also saw this as a opportunity to prove his godly might and status. The fight between the two was evenly matched, Miles even calling Zephyr's strength "otherworldly". During the fight Miles made Zephyr bleed a golden ichor from his mouth due to his barrage of attacks, thus further proving Zephyr is actually descended from gods. Seeking to wrap up the fight quickly Miles used his "maxxed mode" and charges a devastating punch wrapped in his venom which rendered Zephyr unconscious. Miles said this was the hardest punch he had ever thrown seeing somewhat impressed that the demi-god was only knocked out cold and not worse. Zip Zephyr is then left in the battlefield for the NYPD to retrieve him. Zip was incarcerated in the Raft, where he was kept in check with an Inhibitor Collar. While Zip was bemoaning his fate, he was approached by Ares, who offered to help break Zip out and promote him from Theoi to Olympian in exchange for Zip swearing fealty to him and killing Kwaku Anansi's latest herald, Miles. Zip agreed and attacked Miles at the Brooklyn Visions Academy, nearly killing him by sucking the air out of his lungs before being stopped by Thor and Hercules. The battered Zip was then recovered by Ares and War-Cry.

ziran.name: Ziran
ziran.origin: ===Celestial War=== Predating the Multiverse by many times over, Ziran was one of the Celestials from the First Cosmos, the first-ever universe. They rebelled against their creator, the First Firmament, and the Aspirants, shattering the First Cosmos into the Second Cosmos, the first-ever Multiverse. This began the multiversal cycles. The Celestials created and/or appointed many beings to serve them, including but not limited to the Exterminators, Cal-Horra, and the Omegas. Each time the Multiverse ended, the Celestials passed on to the next incarnation of the Multiverse. At some point, the Celestials also began to assign Kings in Black. Although split across the Multiverse, the Celestials' counterparts are interconnected aspects of themselves and not separate beings. Thus, the Ziran of Earth-616 is one aspect of the true Ziran. ===Knull=== Following many multiversal cycles, Ziran and the other Celestials began the creation of the Seventh Cosmos and attempted to recruit Knull, a primordial god of darkness who ruled over the Void that had been formed by the Sixth Cosmos' destruction, to be their King in Black, but he rejected the responsibility. When Knull killed one of Ziran's comrades, the Celestials retaliated by banishing Knull back into the void, though he eventually returned to wage war on them. To oppose him, the Celestials created the Enigma Force. ===Earth-616=== A Celestial that tests the stability of genes and such in the lifeforms they have evolved. He sends them through a series of tests until they are ready to go back to the planet to start their new lives. ===Multiverse=== The Celestials exist across the Multiverse simultaneously. A Celestial's alternate reality selves are actually aspects of the same being. Despite this, their alternate aspects may have very different histories from the ones in the mainstream Marvel Universe. ====Earth-8101==== thumb|none Ziran the Tester was one of the Celestials who visited Earth-8101. ====Earth-9997==== thumb|none Ziran is a member of the Celestial race. Having long since evolved past physical bodies, the Celestials reproduced by impregnating a planet with their essence, which in time would gestate into an infant Celestial. To protect the growing fetus, they would genetically modify the people of said world, greatly enhancing their evolutionary potential and imbuing them with a certain level of aggressiveness. One of these impregnated planets was Earth. After the populace of Earth fully mutated prematurely, Ziran and other Celestials travelled to the world to purge it of all life before they could threaten the infant Celestial. They were met with opposition from Black Bolt on the Moon, Ziran and the Celestials would kill Black Bolt and then set their sights on Earth. On Earth, they would be opposed by Namor and an army of sea creatures, Tony Stark in a giant robotic factor and an army of Iron Men robots, and an army of Asgardians led by Loki. This bought the Earth precious moments for the arrival of "Galactus" (actually Franklin Richards) who was called to Earth by Black Bolt before his death. Galactus was able to fight off the Celestials, and Ziran was one of the Celestials felled in the battle. ====Earth-17628==== thumb|none Ziran the Tester was one of the Celestials who attempted to bring light to the universe but found themselves up against Knull. They were defeated after Knull created the Klyntar to be used against them. It is unknown if Ziran was killed or was one of the few who survived and fled to the farthest reaches of space. ====Earth-21443==== thumb|none Ziran the Tester and other Celestials were briefly seen millions of years in the past, during the time of the Dinosaurs by Kang the Conqueror when he was travelling through the time stream looking for Black Panther. ====Earth-89721==== thumb|none Ziran the Tester was one of the Celestials who came to Earth and judged humanity unworthy. The evolved humans joined their minds in one and killed Arishem the Judge which prompted the other Celestials to leave Earth alone. ====Earth-90251==== thumb|none Ziran and all of the Celestials were killed by Doctor Doom in a battle that lasted 407 years, after Doom gained the power of the Beyonder and the Infinity Gauntlet. ====Earth-90266==== thumb|none Ziran, along with many Abstract Entities, tried to stop Thanos after he activated the Infinity Gauntlet. Ziran's armor was later piloted by Iron Man to fight Thanos, while using it to channel the power Negative Zone. After Thanos was defeated by the New Fantastic Four and Spider-Man acquired the Infinity Gauntlet, all of those killed by Thanos (save Mephisto), were resurrected, including Ziran. ====Earth-95397==== thumb|none Ziran was one of the many Cosmic Beings who assembled to reclaim the Infinity Gauntlet from the Impossible Man. ====Earth-16524==== thumb|none ====Earth-TRN909==== thumb|none Ziran was killed alongside the universe's galactic empires, Galactus, and the other Celestials by Annihilus during hi

zirksu.origin: thumb|left|130px|Zirksu as Diabolik Zirksu was a member of the Skrull army that operated during the late 50s and an enemy of the first 3-D Man. He was first seen in the Skrull ship that kidnapped the NASA pilot Chuck Chandler, while he was testing the latest NASA's prototype, the XF-13. Discovering that Chuck has become the 3-D Man, he decided to assume the identity of Diabolik, a communist spy, and collaborate with the Russians to catch 3-D Man. Eventually 3-D Man defeated the spies and Zirksu revealed his identity to Chuck, but managed to escape. left|84px|Zirksu as Boss Buzz He then assumed the identity of Boss Buzz, the leader of a street gang. Thanks to his Skrull-sensing powers, 3-D Man found him and easily defeated his gang, but Zirksu escaped, assuming another identity: Doc Rock, a DJ. Thanks to this identity he gave a special guitar to a young rockstar, Vince Rivers, acting as his manager. The guitar was actually a Skrull experimental weapon, which could alter teenagers' behavior. 3-D Man helped the police to calm down the teenagers and Vince was arrested, even if the criminal was in fact Doc Rock. thumb|left|80px|Zirksu as Doc Rock Zirksu then assumed the identity of the vice-president Richard Nixon, to convince unsuccessful scientist Eric Sinkovitz that 3-D Man was actually a red spy. Sinkovitz used his scientific experiments to become the Cold Warrior and started a battle with 3-D Man, who defeated him. Then Zirksu, disappointed for his failure, abandoned Nixon's identity to take a less notable appearance, and stopped trying to catch 3-D Man.
